intended_object: The closed subgroup scheme of GLₙ over ℤ generated by the weight (split) torus and the Kostant root subgroups 𝔾ₐ → GLₙ indexed by S. It comes from the Kostant ℤ-form of a ℚ-Lie algebra representation and a ℤ-lattice M with basis b. This is what the docstring and the module documentation say: it is the scheme-level candidate for a Borel subgroup when S is a positive system.
explanation:
The body takes the coordinate Hopf algebra ℤ[GLₙ] and divides it by `kostantTorusSubsystemDefiningIdeal`. That ideal is `commonKernelHopfIdeal` of the coordinate maps for the selected root subgroups and the weight torus, defined as the supremum of all Hopf ideals that lie in every kernel. It then takes Spec of the quotient as a group object over Spec ℤ.

A closed subgroup scheme of GLₙ is the same thing as a Hopf ideal of ℤ[GLₙ]. A family of morphisms factors through such a subgroup exactly when the family kills its ideal. So the largest Hopf ideal killed by the family gives the smallest closed subgroup scheme containing the images, which is the generated closed subgroup scheme. The library proves this minimality property in `kostantTorusSubsystemClosedSubgroup_le_iff`. Using the largest Hopf ideal inside the kernels, rather than the plain intersection of kernels, is the right choice, because that intersection need not be a Hopf ideal.

The setting (GLₙ over ℤ, a lattice with a basis, a Lie algebra over ℚ) is the one the construction needs: Kostant ℤ-forms and Chevalley group schemes live over ℤ. Mathlib has no matching general notion of a "closed subgroup scheme generated by morphisms" or of Hopf ideals that this should be stated through. The definition is therefore faithful at its natural generality.
